original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected reproduction command and choose a single replay stage for profiling.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Can scripts/partial_swap/shared.py:SharedPointCircuit.verify emit the same circuit_sha256 digest lines (and the same support/topology assertion checks) without per-node json.dumps, so partial-swap verify receipts stay fieldwise identical while certificates/partial-swap-network.json updates only the shared.py source_sha256 pin?
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one measured replay bottleneck with before/after wall time and retained checks. Expertise override selected verifier-engineering after open tooling PRs #1984/#1994 left the same hand-rolled digest pattern available on the distinct partial-swap fork of SharedPointCircuit (scripts/partial_swap/shared.py), which still called json.dumps per active node. Profiling named that digest stream as about half of h=46 verify time. Mask/closed-form ExclusionCircuit and DisjointTensor support rewrites (#2001) and the canonical shared_point_circuit.py digest object (#1994) are deliberately out of scope.
bottleneck_link: Side result on review throughput: partial-swap producers, skip-strip graphs and related historical packages import partial_swap.shared.SharedPointCircuit.verify. A faster identical digest does not change kappa or the binding complex supplier.
stop_rule: Ship an equivalence-preserving partial_swap SharedPointCircuit.verify digest change with frozen baseline, identical receipts on the historical h=46 circuit, pin-only certificate refresh, registered replay and a measured before/after median. Do not reopen mathematical screens, rewrite ExclusionCircuit/DisjointTensor support masks, or edit scripts/shared_point_circuit.py.
evidence: PASS_PARTIAL_SWAP_DIGEST via research/partial-swap-digest/verify.py (also under -O); PASS_IDENTICAL_PARTIAL_SWAP_DIGEST_RECEIPTS via benchmark.py; certificates/partial-swap-network.json changes only scripts/partial_swap/shared.py in source_sha256.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for orientation, overlap search, profiling, implementation, packaging, benchmarking and writing. Not independent human peer review.

open_questions.question: Should research packages that pin live scripts/partial_swap/shared.py bytes (for example copied-fixed / skip-strip provenance) refresh that one SHA-256 entry after this equivalence-preserving digest rewrite?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Those provenance packages bind working-tree bytes of shared.py; leaving old pins keeps this tooling PR focused, but a later full provenance replay on main would see a hash mismatch until refreshed.
open_questions.first_step: Open a dedicated provenance follow-up that only rewrites the shared.py entry after confirming circuit_sha256 identity.
open_questions.blocked_by: Pin repair outside certificates/partial-swap-network.json is outside this tooling change.

open_questions.question: Is partial_swap.shared.SharedPointCircuit.__init__ merge/lookup construction worth a separate identical-receipt rewrite?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Bit-compression and large partial-swap builds still spend substantial wall time constructing the shared-point DAG; that is a different object from the verify digest stream measured here.
open_questions.first_step: Profile SharedPointCircuit(46).__init__ alone and compare against the verify residual after this digest change.
open_questions.blocked_by: Out of this session's stop rule; verify digests were the measured bottleneck.
